newsitem.title: HONG KONG: KDB Securities details EBRD won bond issue. [CORRECTED 13:13 GMT]
newsitem.headline: KDB Securities details EBRD won bond issue. [CORRECTED 13:13 GMT]

text.p: KDB Securities on Tuesday detailed terms of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development's (EBRD) debut won-denominated bond issue.
The EBRD launched a 94.8 billion won bond issue on Monday, split into tranches for international and domestic investors.
KDB Securities was lead manager for the domestic tranche and joint lead manager with Merrill Lynch International for the international tranche.
Both tranches mature on May 2, 1997 and pay a semi-annual coupon of 10.0 percent. The bonds are available in denominations of one million and 100 million Korean won.
Governing law is Korean and the payment date is May 2, 1997.
The 71.1 billion domestic tranche was priced at 92.57 to yield 12.02 percent (corrects from 12.2 percent), or 63 basis points below three-year bank guaranteed Korean corporate bonds.
Nine financial institutions participated in the domestic tranche of the transaction in addition to lead manager KDB Securities.
Samsung Securities acted as co-lead manager.
Tong Yank Securities, Shin Young Securities, Hanwha Securities, Dongsuh Securities and Sunkyong Securities are co-managers.
Korea Housing and Commercial Bank, Hannuri Salomon Securities and Nomura Securities' Seoul branch acted as underwriters.
The 23.7 billion won international tranche was priced at 100.25 percent to yield 9.935 percent on a semi-annual basis.
In addition to lead managers KDB Securities and Merrill Lynch International, four investment banks participated.
HSBC Markets and Oakreed Financial Services acted as co-lead managers, while ING Barings and Tokyo-Mitsubishi International (HK) were co-managers.
